 Rajesh Kumar Gupta A

 State Of Uttarakhand & Anr.
Re  O R D E R Leave granted.
Being aggrieved by the order dated 29.11.2018 passed in Criminal Misc. Application No.414/2008 by the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital, the appellant has preferred this appeal.

entities.text: High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Briefly stated the facts are that the appellant had assailed the invocation of Section 8 read with Section 22 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short NDPS Act) and Section 4 read with section 7 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act,
1954 as well as Sections 147, 323, 504, 506, 353, 332, 224, 427 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code (for short IPC) and Section 7 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, as against him.

entities.text: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text:
Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act,
1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: At this stage itself, it may be mentioned that the appellant is an Ayurvedic Doctor practicing medicine in Neeraj Clinic Private Limited.

That there was a raid conducted by the police team on 03.08.2004 at the aforesaid clinic and during the course of raid allegedly certain psychotropic substances were recovered in a large quantity from his clinic.
Therefore, FIR being Case Crime No.303/2004 at Police Station, Rishikesh was lodged against the appellant and other accused invoking the aforesaid Sections.

The appellant sought for quashing of the criminal complaint as well as proceedings by filing a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short Cr.P.C.)
before the High Court.
Initially the said petition was partly allowed and the invocation of the offences against the appellant in respect of the NDPS Act only was quashed.

As against the said order, SLP(Crl.) No.10144/2009 was filed before this Court which was remanded by order dated 13.01.2017, by observing that the High Court without independently examining whether an offence under NDPS Act had been made out, had simply quashed the proceedings only on the observations Rajesh Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Uttarakhand on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55375695/
1 of the said Court that prima facie the provisions of NDPS Act would not apply.

entities.text: Rajesh Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Uttarakhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Court set aside the order of the High Court and remanded the matter to the High Court for a fresh consideration.
By the impugned order dated 29.11.2018, the High Court dismissed the application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. filed by the appellant herein.
Hence, this appeal.
We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent-State and perused the material on record.

During the course of submissions, our attention was drawn to the fact that during the pendency of this case before this Court the appellant was convicted of the offences under the IPC and the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954.

entities.text: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, no trial in respect of the offences alleged under the NDPS Act was commenced.
That being aggrieved by the order of conviction, the appellant had preferred Criminal Appeal No.164/2017 and Criminal Appeal No.1/2018 before the 5th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun.
By judgment dated 17.02.2018, the said appeals have been allowed and the appellant is acquitted of the offences alleged against him under the aforesaid Acts.
However, the fact remains that as against the offences alleged against the appellant under Section 8 read with Section 22 of the NDPS Act, no trial has commenced.

In this regard, the contention of learned counsel for the appellant was that in view of the acquittal of the appellant under the provisions of the aforesaid Acts, no offences could have been made out as against the appellant under the provisions of the Sections 8 and 22 of the NDPS Act also.

Therefore,
this Court may set aside the impugned order and allow the application filed by the appellant herein and quash the FIR as against Sections 8 and 22 of the NDPS Act also.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent-State supported the impugned order and however,
submitted that in view of the acquittal of the appellant herein, the High Court may reconsider the application filed by the appellant herein seeking quashing of the FIR with regard to Sections 8 and 22 of the NDPS Act in light of the acquittal of the appellant in so far as the other provisions in the respective Acts are concerned.

Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of the material on record, we find that in view of the acquittal of the appellant under the provisions of the IPC as well as the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 and since the proceedings under Sections 8 and 22 of the NDPS Act have not yet commenced, it would be just and proper for the High Court to reconsider the Criminal Misc. Application No.414/2008 filed by the appellant herein in light of the acquittal of the appellant.

entities.text: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In fact, the appellant ought to have brought to the notice of the High Court, the judgment of acquittal dated 17.02.2018, which would have been a relevant consideration for the High Court to have taken while disposing of the application filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: In the circumstances, we set aside the impugned order dated 29.11.2018 and remand the matter to the High Court to reconsider Criminal Misc. Application No.414/2008 in light of the acquittal of the appellant under the provisions of the aforesaid two Acts and in light of Sections 8 and 22 of the NDPS Act.
The appeal is allowed and disposed of in the aforesaid terms.

Since the appellant had an interim stay of the operation of the impugned order which has continued till date, we observe that till the disposal of the criminal Misc. Application No.414/2008, no proceeding in respect of Section 8 read with Section 22 of the NDPS Act shall not commence.

In view of the aforesaid directions, the High Court is requested to dispose of Criminal Misc.
Application No.414/2008 expeditiously.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
